recipes.name: Honey Apricot Pork Chops
ingredients_raw: Kosher salt and fresh cracked pepper to taste
4 fresh apricots, pitted and cut into wedges
3 cloves garlic, minced, or to taste

steps.text: Pat pork chops dry with paper towels, then sprinkle both sides with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add chops and brown well, about 5 minutes per side. Stir in honey, apricots, and garlic; cover and simmer until pork is tender, about 8 minutes. An instant-read thermometer, inserted into the center, should read at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).
Serve chops topped with apricots and pan juices. Garnish with parsley.

raw_recipe.headline: Honey Apricot Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Honey-apricot pork chops are simmered to tender perfection in this simple recipe that you can tell everyone had you working in the kitchen all day long!

review.reviewBody: I'm not a pork chop fan but these were really good. I seasoned the chops with a heavy dose of chili powder since we like a kick in our food. I also did not have fresh apricots or canned, so I used apricot preserves instead. I will definitely make this again..very easy and quick!

I have now made this twice. The first time, I followed the recipe as written. I liked the flavor, but the pork chops were very dry after browning 5 mins. on each side, and the honey very quickly turned black during simmering. This second time, I used thin-sliced pork chops and only browned them for about 1.5 mins. on each side. To simmer them, I mixed 1 cup of apricot preserves together with the honey, then added that to my skillet.... this way, I got much more apricot flavor, and I got the honey flavor without it turning dark and ugly. I also think it helped with keeping the pork chops moist. Then, I added my quartered fresh apricot wedges to the simmering mixture for just the last 1-2 minutes..... this was enough to warm them, but not turn them to a cooked mush. I served the pork chops and fresh apricots over rice, with all the delicious juices spooned on top. THIS I will make again!
**ADDENDUM: TONIGHT I MADE IT USING PEACHES, AS THEY WERE ABUNDANT AT THE FARM MARKET, AND PEACH PRESERVES..... I THINK THEY WORK EQUALLY AS WELL AS APRICOTS! :) **

We really loved this! Don’t let the paper plate fool you — this is a classy dish! I used fresh apricots but first put the sauce ingredients on a saucepan on low for about 15 min to get the fruit with the honey and garlic to blend together. I then sautéed the chops 4 min on one side and 3 on the other, added the warmed sauce to the pan and removed from heat and covered for 10 min. Chops were perfect!

I didn’t have fresh apricots either so I used canned, drained but saved the juice and added a little of it to the end to make more juices for the rice to soak up. I also added a little cayenne to one side of each chop to give it some kick...sweet and spicy over rice and served with asparagus. This a keeper for sure. It’s easy, pretty quick to fix and delicious. My guys loved it.

Used canned apricots in own juice put all in pan after took browned chops out and simmered to reduce some of the liquid and scrap of the good little bits. Everything else the same except had only two bone in chops but there are only two of us and I can't eat much meat. Meat needed more cooking time. Must depend on thickness of chops. Wonderful apricot flavor. I had some precooked rice an just tossed it in at the simmering stage to be sure it was warm. Served with green beans. Will make again.

Fresh apricots are just coming in season so I bought them a few days ahead to ripen. We love apples with pork but the apricots were a delight as well. This is easy and would be a great company dish when you don’t want to fuss all day in the kitchen! Edit: 3/8/25: Apricots are not in season and I didn’t have apricot preserves as a reviewer suggested but I did have orange marmalade! My chops were thin, so I browned 2 salt and peppered chops for 2 minutes per side, added 1/2 cup marmalade mixed with 1 tbsp honey, covered and added 1 sliced and peeled Granny Smith apple during the 2 minutes Yum over rice with broccoli and cornbread!

I substituted 1/2 a sweet red onion, sliced, for the garlic, sauteeing it for a few minutes in the olive oil before browning the meat. I also substituted 4 (peeled, sliced) peaches for the apricots, as there were no fresh apricots available. When the meat was done, I removed and covered it and reduced the sauce a bit before serving. The resulting dish was delicious, and went well with green beans and brown rice. I look forward to next summer's apricots so I can try the original. Note: no extra honey was needed.

Yes, after reading reviews I included many of the suggestions. No fresh apricots available, so substituted both preserves and canned apricots. I only had mango infused honey which I think only added to the yumminess.
A big deviation was the addition of tamari, low sodium version and a small slurry of cornstarch to thicken up the sauce. We all loved it. Quick and easy.

I used thick pork chops and it took a bit longer. The recipe did not specify what size. I loved it when I cut them thin and soaked them in the juice. I would add more honey and didn't have fresh apricots so I used canned. Pat dry them & used the whole can & glad I did.

The flavors were great, but following the directions as written produced pork that was too well done for my taste. After reading some reviews, I also substituted preserves instead of fresh fruit. 
The second time I made this, I seared the meat for about 4 minutes per side. After searing the second side, I removed the pork from the pan and poured in the sauce, simmering until it thickened up a bit. Then I returned the meat to the pan and simmered for only 5 or so minutes.

We really liked this. We had steamed asparagus with a warm lemon vinaigrette as she suggested and it was a beautiful counter-point. Brilliant. 
Yes, once the chops were done I took them out and mashed up the peaches so that they were more of a sauce. (store did not have ripe apricots but our Colorado peaches were nice and ready)
This recipe was so easy and delicious. Pork was nice and juicy!!
Super easy. The apricots and honey balance out the pork chops well.
My family loved it!
Easy to make very tasty this is a keeper

We enjoyed the recipe, the chops we used were poor quality..
We will make again with different chops
Love it. Sweet with out being too sweet and fast and easy to make!
Wonderful and so easy. I spent 6 hours painting our deck with my wife. While she showered, I prepared dinner! She was amazed at a dinner that took 35 minutes to prepare but was so delicious!

I don't usually eat pork so must admit I had trouble getting the cooking times correct. First time it was too pink inside so gave it 2 more minutes which then overcooked it. Anyway the savory flavors just weren't there. I used fresh very ripe apricots and followed recipe exactly. Won't make it again
We loved this recipe, I did make one change to it, I omitted the parsley as a garnish. It was so easy to make, and tasted really wonderful.
